name: The Duchess
temperament: Swings between extremes. At home she is savage, careless and rough with her child. In society she is cloying, clinging and agreeable, and crushes every exchange into a moral. Underneath both she is a survivor who bends to whoever holds power.

traits.description: Rude to a polite child, harsh to the baby, and quick to hand him off to a stranger.

evidence.quote: “You don’t know much,” said the Duchess; “and that’s a fact.”
Speak roughly to your little boy
evidence.note: Her lullaby is a recipe for harshness.

evidence.quote: flinging the baby at her as she spoke
evidence.note: Hands off her child to go and play croquet.

traits.description: At court she is suddenly affectionate and agreeable, presses close to Alice, and agrees with everything.

evidence.quote: You can’t think how glad I am to see you again, you dear old thing!
evidence.note: A complete change from the kitchen.

evidence.quote: who seemed ready to agree to everything that Alice said
evidence.note: Agreeable to the point of emptiness.

traits.description: Turns every remark into a moral, however irrelevant.

evidence.quote: Everything’s got a moral, if only you can find it.
Be what you would seem to be
evidence.note: A moral she herself does not live by.

traits.trait: Dismissive of a child's right to think
traits.description: Belittles Alice's inner life even while fawning over her.

evidence.quote: Just about as much right,” said the Duchess, “as pigs have to fly
evidence.note: Her answer to 'I've a right to think'.

traits.trait: Brave behind the scenes, cowardly face to face
traits.description: Has reportedly boxed the Queen's ears, yet collapses and flees the moment she meets the Queen's frown.

evidence.quote: the Duchess began in a low, weak voice
evidence.note: Face to face with the Queen.

evidence.quote: The Duchess took her choice, and was gone in a moment.

motivation.core: Standing: to hold her rank and her head. She is gracious when it costs nothing, savage when unobserved, and off like a shot when the Queen turns on her.
motivation.want: To be seen as a lady of good sense and good morals; to be on good terms with the court and play croquet with the Queen.
motivation.fear: The Queen's sentence and the loss of her position.

evidence.quote: I must go and get ready to play croquet with the Queen
evidence.note: The royal invitation comes before her baby.
What hangs over her at the croquet.

shifts.to: fawning society guest, freshly let out of 'prison' (ch008-p70) and eager to please
abandoning her instantly to save herself from the Queen

habits.habit: Answers with a moral: 'and the moral of that is—'
Digs her sharp chin into Alice's shoulder while talking
Tucks her arm into Alice's and squeezes up close
Tosses and jerks the baby about while singing to it
Sits on a three-legged stool in the middle of the smoke, heedless of the chaos

decision_pattern: Reads the power in the room and matches it: rude to people beneath her, sweet to useful company, gone when the stronger party arrives. She rationalises everything afterwards with a moral.

taboos.taboo: Never defies the Queen face to face
taboos.rationale: The reported ear-boxing is never staged. In person she speaks in 'a low, weak voice' and flees.
taboos.qa_check: No on-screen confrontation where the Duchess stands up to the Queen.

taboos.taboo: Never shows real tenderness to the baby
taboos.rationale: Her care is rough and performative, which is what makes the pig-baby beat land (SUP-006).

taboos.taboo: Never admits a child has a mind of her own
taboos.rationale: 'As much right as pigs have to fly'.
taboos.qa_check: She must not concede a point to Alice on its merits. She only agrees emptily.

taboos.taboo: Never actually harms the baby or Alice
taboos.rationale: Realistic staging: the baby-tossing and baby-throwing are shown as careless handling (a fling into Alice's arms), never as injury, in line with the SUP-006 continuous-shot transformation and the non-violent tone (SUP-014 spirit).
taboos.reason: A designed staging limit on a sourced rough behaviour.
taboos.qa_check: No blow to the baby on screen. 'Beat him when he sneezes' stays in the song.

facade.surface: A gracious, affectionate, morally improving lady (ch009)
facade.true_self: A harsh, self-serving survivor, as seen in the kitchen (ch006)
facade.note: The audience sees the true self first. The ch009 charm should read as suspicious, a mask Alice half-sees through (ch009-p02: she hopes it was 'only the pepper'). Her flight from the Queen (ch009-p33) confirms it.

waking_life_embodiment.adult_trait: The adult of moral lessons and rough nursery care: the aunt, nurse or visiting lady who preaches pat morals at a child, crushes her 'right to think', neglects or roughly handles small children, and turns sweet in company.
waking_life_embodiment.waking_source: Victorian nursery practice and the moral recitation-pieces of Alice's schoolroom (world.json cp-lessons; culture.json moral-verse customs). The Duchess's household is a dream invention (FAC-duchess-household), not a recast real person (ruling 5.3 B light doubling).

evidence.quote: Speak roughly to your little boy
evidence.note: A parody of nursery moral verse.

waking_life_embodiment.reason: A design reading grounded in world.json cp-lessons and the source's parody of moral verse. She is explicitly not a doubling of any waking person.

performance_keynote: Plain, poorer gentry dress (index performer_concept). Heavy, sneezing and slapdash in the kitchen. At court, over-close, with a dig of the chin and a syrupy voice that fades to a whisper the moment the Queen appears.

consistency_flags.flag: She boxed the Queen's ears (ch008-p40, reported) yet cannot even speak up to her (ch009-p31-p33)
consistency_flags.note: This is in the source and not resolved by it. Recommended reading: the ear-boxing was a flash of temper (the pepper-kitchen Duchess) that now has her under sentence, and her fawning in ch009 comes from fear after that mistake. Flagged for logic-qa. Not patched in the bible.

reason: Behaviours are sourced. The embodiment and the non-injury staging limit are design choices.
